Definition: gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative
KeyPassages: Genesis 1:1; Exodus 1:17; Leviticus 2:13; Numbers 6:7; Deuteronomy 1:6; Joshua 1:9
BiblicalUsage: ʼĕlôhîym means God. In Genesis 1:1, the text says "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth." In Exodus 1:17, the text says "But the midwives feared God."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that ʼĕlôhîym matters because God is who He says He is, and His name carries everything He is. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedBooks: Genesis; Exodus; Leviticus; Numbers; Deuteronomy; Joshua
RelatedEvents: Creation; Moses' Birth and Flight to Midian; Joshua Commissioned to Lead Israel
